## Fee cascade

<!-- Edge cases in three-tier fee resolution (site → partnerAccount → settings) -->

### 2026-10-05: "Waive all fees" writes 0% account-level ServiceFee rows, not a CustomSubscription field
tags: entities=payment,subscription,service-fee · files=apps/admin/app/partners/[id]/actions.ts,apps/admin/app/fees/actions.ts
**Problem:** The partner page (`/partners/[id]`) carries three different account-level levers and
recall leads conflate them: a session note claimed "waiveAllFees sets customSubscription to zero".
It does not. A fee override is recognised purely by which of `ServiceFee.accountId` / `siteId` is
populated (both null = the Settings/tier default), so a waiver must be a *fee row*, not a
subscription field.
**Solution:** `waiveAllServiceFees` (`apps/admin/app/partners/[id]/actions.ts#waiveAllServiceFees`)
loads every `ServiceCode`, resolves the `Settings` row by the partner's country (falling back to the
first Settings row — error `'No Settings configured'` if none), then upserts one `chargeType:
'percentage', percentage: 0` account fee per code through the shared `saveServiceFee`
(`apps/admin/app/fees/actions.ts`), keyed on existing `getFeesByAccount` rows so re-running is a
no-op. The other two levers are separate: `upsertCustomSubscription` / `setFeatureOverride` write
`CustomSubscription` (`maxSites`, `featureOverrides` validated against `SUBSCRIPTION_FEATURES`), and
`grantPartnerPromotion` / `revokePartnerPromotion` call `@repo/data/promotion-db` (the launch offer's
30-day clock starts at the first live paid booking, not at grant).
**Prevention:** When touching partner-level pricing, decide which lever first: fee amount → `ServiceFee`
account row (per service code, so a "waiver" is N rows); plan limits/features → `CustomSubscription`;
time-boxed commission holiday → promotion. Tests for this page mock `@repo/data/promotion-db` via
`apps/admin/__mocks__/@repo/data/promotion-db.ts`, while fee rows go through the Prisma mock's
`serviceFee` / `serviceCode` / `settings` tables. Pricing display: `PRICING_TIERS` commission values
carry decimals (e.g. 1.5%) — format from the constant, never an integer literal.

## Partner & site overrides

<!-- Admin-only overrides of partner/site state that other surfaces also write (payment provider, tax identity, brand) -->

### 2026-10-07: Admin site-provider override is readiness-gated and can be undone by the partner's next provider sync
tags: entities=site,payment,partnerAccount · files=apps/admin/app/sites/actions.ts,packages/data/src/payment-providers/readiness.ts,packages/data/src/payment-providers/selection.ts · track=028
**Problem:** `updatePaymentProvider` used to accept `'stripe'` unchecked and verify only a Mollie
token (the "Mollie token verification" still described in `apps/admin/CLAUDE.md` is stale). Two
things were non-obvious after the track-028 rewrite: (1) the override writes only the *effective*
`Site.paymentProvider`, never the partner's *selected* `PartnerAccount.paymentProvider`; (2) it is
not durable — `syncEffectiveProvider` (`packages/data/src/payment-providers/selection.ts`), called
from the partner app after any connect/disconnect/selection change, runs `site.updateMany` across
**every** site of the account to one provider derived from the account's selection + readiness.
**Solution:** `apps/admin/app/sites/actions.ts#updatePaymentProvider` now requires
`isSelectableProvider` (mollie | viva | stripe) and `providerReadiness(toReadinessAccount(account),
provider).ready` for the site owner's account (Mollie = token + onboarding `'completed'`; Viva =
merchant id + `'verified'`; Stripe = `chargesEnabled`), erroring with `'<Label> is not ready for this
partner (<status>)'`; a site with no `PartnerAccount` reports `not_connected` instead of throwing.
Per `effectiveProviderFor` (`readiness.ts`), a site override survives a sync only while the partner's
selected provider is *not* ready and the overridden site is the account's oldest (its provider seeds
`previousEffective`).
**Prevention:** Treat the override as a repair tool, not a configuration: to move a partner
permanently, change the selection on the partner side. In tests, readiness is driven by the
`prisma.site.findUnique` mock returning `{ user: { partnerAccount: { …READINESS_SELECT fields } } }`
(see `apps/admin/app/sites/actions.test.ts`), and assert `prisma.partnerAccount.update` is never
called. Readiness criteria live in `@repo/data/payment-providers/readiness` — don't restate them in
the action.

### 2026-10-08: Tax region decides Veri*factu scope; an unknown province is "out of scope", not an error, downstream
tags: entities=partnerAccount,invoice,tax-region · files=apps/admin/app/partners/[id]/actions.ts,packages/data/src/tax/regime.ts,apps/admin/app/verifactu/page.tsx · track=026
**Problem:** A Spanish partner produced order receipts with no Veri*factu QR and no AEAT records.
The suspect was an invalid NIF; the cause was an empty `PartnerAccount.taxRegion`.
`resolveTaxRegime` (`packages/data/src/tax/regime.ts#resolveTaxRegime`) returns `NONE` for an ES
issuer with an empty *or unrecognised* region (it once fell through to `ES_VERIFACTU`, which would
have filed a foral taxpayer's records to AEAT), so a typo or a blank silently removes the partner
from filing rather than failing anything. `taxRegion` had no writer at all until track 026 7a — "set
it in admin" was impossible.
**Solution:** `apps/admin/app/partners/[id]/actions.ts#setPartnerTaxIdentity` is the only writer: it
uppercases/trims, rejects anything not in `isKnownEsRegion` with an explanatory error, writes
`taxRegion` + `isTestAccount`, and returns the resolved `regime` so the UI states the consequence.
The read-only `/verifactu` ops page (`apps/admin/app/verifactu/page.tsx`) lists Spanish issuers with
no province (`needsTaxRegion`), invoices with no record, records AEAT accepted with errors, records
parked on AEAT's `4112` authorisation gate, and certificate expiry read from the cert itself.
**Prevention:** Debug "no QR / no records" by checking `taxRegion` + `country === 'ES'` before the
tax id. Invoice merchant tax ids are stamped at invoice creation (a NIF change affects new invoices
only), but the regime is resolved live — setting the region makes existing receipts render a QR.
Never add a "fix/void record" button to `/verifactu`: corrections are deliberately CLI-only
(`verifactu:subsanar`, `verifactu:anular`).

## Sudo auth

<!-- Unexpected behaviors in the requireSudo guard, session edge cases -->

### 2026-10-11: Feature flags resolve sudo → env → per-account → global row → default, so flags cannot gate entitlements
tags: entities=feature-flag,subscription,partnerAccount · files=apps/admin/app/flags/actions.ts,packages/data/src/flags.ts · track=021
**Problem:** The `/flags` page looks like a generic on/off switch, but `resolveFlag`
(`packages/data/src/flags.ts`) has five tiers, first match wins: sudo bypass (only when the caller
passes `isSudo: true` to `getFlagStates`) → `FF_<UPPER_SNAKE>` env var → `account_feature_flag`
row (track 021 P5) → global `feature_flag` row → per-`VERCEL_ENV` default from `FLAG_REGISTRY`. Two
consequences bite: sudo users see every flagged feature regardless of DB state (so a flag can never
enforce a paid tier — use `CustomSubscription.featureOverrides` / subscription entitlements for that),
and an env override makes the admin toggle a recorded-but-ineffective write (the row's `source` says
`env`).
**Solution:** `apps/admin/app/flags/actions.ts` exposes global `setFlag` / `clearFlag`
(`setFlagOverride(name, enabled | null)`) and per-customer `setFlagForAccount` /
`clearFlagForAccount` (`searchPartners` finds the account by email/name). **Clearing ≠ setting
false**: a cleared account row follows the global flag again, a `false` row pins the customer off
even when the global default later flips on. Every action validates `name in FLAG_REGISTRY`; adding
a flag is one registry entry and the page lists it automatically. Current registry: `assistant`
(off everywhere, pilot per account, always on for sudo), `devices`, `restaurants`.
**Prevention:** Before wiring any gate on a flag, ask whether sudo must *not* bypass it — if so it is
an entitlement, not a flag. When a flag "doesn't change", read the row's `source` (`sudo` / `env` /
`account` / `db` / `default`) before touching the DB. Tests mock `@repo/data/flags` wholesale
(`apps/admin/app/flags/actions.test.ts`) — resolution order is asserted in `packages/data`, not here.

## Test failures & fixes

<!-- Non-obvious mock setups; known bugs the tests deliberately assert against -->

### 2026-10-06: Admin has no Prisma mock-contract test — a new model is missing until an action calls it
tags: entities=prisma-mock,lead,feature-flag · files=apps/admin/__mocks__/@repo/data/PrismaCient.ts,apps/partner/app/test/mock-contract.test.ts · track=027
**Problem:** Adding the `Lead` model to the schema broke the partner app's `mock-contract.test.ts`;
admin (and user) have no such test, so `apps/admin/__mocks__/@repo/data/PrismaCient.ts` only grows
when a test fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'findUnique')` on a model the
mock never declared. The mock's table list in `apps/admin/CLAUDE.md` § Mocking is already behind the
file (it now also carries `device`, `customSubscription`, `platformPreference`, `featureFlag`,
`impersonationLog`).
**Solution:** Admin tests use two mocking tiers, and the choice is made by the action, not the test:
an action that calls `prisma.<model>.*` directly needs that model (and each method it uses) added to
the manual Prisma mock; an action that goes through a `@repo/data/<module>` service is mocked at the
module (`vi.mock('@repo/data/leads')`, `vi.mock('@repo/data/flags')`, or a file under
`__mocks__/@repo/data/` such as `settlement.ts`, `promotion-db.ts`). The leads, flags and promotion
actions take the second route, which is why none of `lead`, `accountFeatureFlag` or the promotion
model exist in the Prisma mock.
**Prevention:** When writing a new admin action against a new model, prefer a `@repo/data` service
+ module mock (the test then asserts the forwarded arguments, as in `flags/actions.test.ts`); only
extend the Prisma mock when the action genuinely reads/writes Prisma itself, and extend it in the same
commit as the action. `requireSudo` tests always need `prisma.user.findUnique` → `{ sudo: true }` in
addition to the auth session (`authenticateAsSudo()`), because every action re-reads `User.sudo`.
